claude_only.name: Which purl type, namespace and name uniquely address this component in its ecosystem of record?
What distinguishes the project-level identity of this component from the identity of one specific release?
Which normalization rules must be applied to the coordinate before two identities are treated as equal?
Which registry or namespace authority allocates this name, and may the name be reassigned after removal?
Which additional identifier schemes are asserted for this component, and by which asserting party?
What evidence supports each cross-scheme mapping, and is it one-to-one, many-to-one or unverified?
How is a conflicting or over-broad identifier match handled when it produces false vulnerability hits?
Which identifier scheme is authoritative for which downstream use case?
Which cryptographic digests, computed over which exact byte streams, address the released artifacts?
What verification procedure is required before these bytes are consumed from an untrusted source?
Which digest algorithms are accepted for this ecosystem and which are deprecated or forbidden?
How does an immutable artifact digest relate to the mutable registry tag or channel that pointed to it?
Which versioning scheme governs this component's version strings, and was that scheme declared or inferred?
How are two versions of this component ordered, and how are pre-release and build metadata treated in that ordering?
Is the published content for a given version immutable, and what mechanism enforces that?
How is this version string represented when exchanged with a tool that assumes a different version scheme?
Which distinct distribution artifacts make up this release, and are any of them optional?
What is the primary purpose and packaging form of each artifact in the release?
Which artifact must be selected for a given target platform, and which metadata drives that selection?
Does each variant carry its own identifier and digest, or do all variants share the release identity?
Which dependencies does this component declare, and under which version constraint expression for each?
What is the scope of each declared dependency, and does it reach the distributed artifact at all?
Which declared dependencies are conditional on platform, feature flag or optional extra?
Is the dependency linked statically, dynamically or used only as a tool, and does that change obligations?
Which resolver, resolver version and registry state produced this closure?
At which instant was the closure resolved, and can it be reproduced from the recorded inputs?
What is the complete transitive component set, and which members are direct rather than transitive?
How complete is the recorded closure, and which parts are explicitly declared unknown?
Which files or subpaths does the released artifact contain, and which of them are third-party code?
What evidence identifies bundled code that is not declared in the dependency manifest?
Which contained subpath is referenced when only part of the component is used?
How do contained subcomponents inherit or override the parent component's licence and provenance?
From which ancestor component, upstream release or revision was this component derived?
Which patches, commits or variant changes were applied to the ancestor to produce this component?
Is this component a fork, a rebuild, a repackaging or an unmodified redistribution?
What confidence attaches to the pedigree chain, and what evidence supports it?
Which agent originated, which supplied and which distributed this component release?
Which role holder is authoritative for security contact and vulnerability response for this component?
How was each role assertion obtained, and is it self-declared or independently verified?
How does a repackager, mirror or internal rebuild change the supply chain seen by a downstream consumer?
Which source repository and exact revision correspond to this released artifact?
What links the distributed artifact to that revision beyond a self-declared repository URL?
What is recorded when no source is available or the source link cannot be verified?
Which qualifier or external reference carries the source location in each exchange representation?
Which build platform, build type and external parameters produced this artifact?
When did the build start and finish, and how do those instants relate to publication?
Which resolved dependencies and byproducts were recorded for the build, and how complete are they?
Which provenance assurance level is claimed, and what concrete evidence supports the claim?
Is the attestation subject digest identical to the digest of the artifact actually distributed?
Which signatures or attestation envelopes cover this artifact, and which identity signed each?
Which verification policy must pass before the component is admitted, and what happens on failure?
When was each signature made, when does the trust material expire, and how is verification-at-time recorded?
On what basis may an unsigned or unverifiable component be accepted, and who authorises that?
What licence expression is declared by the supplier for this component release?
What licence has been concluded after review, and which agent made that determination?
Which operator semantics apply, and which option has been selected under a disjunctive expression?
How are unlicensed, ambiguous or unasserted licence cases represented and escalated?
Which attribution, notice and source-offer obligations attach to redistributing this component?
Which copyright statements and notice texts must be reproduced, and where were they taken from?
How do obligations differ between static linking, dynamic linking and unmodified redistribution?
What record proves the obligations were satisfied for a specific distribution?
What support period has the responsible manufacturer determined for products containing this component?
Which regulator, market and legal instrument imposes obligations on this component's use?
How and when is the end of the support period communicated to the purchaser?
Which due-diligence step was performed before integrating this third-party or open-source component?
Which component data fields must be disclosed, to whom, and in which machine-readable form?
Which reporting deadlines apply once a vulnerability in this component is actively exploited?
Who is entitled to receive the component disclosure, and under what confidentiality terms?
What is disclosed when component contents are commercially sensitive or genuinely unknown?
What is the current published state of this release in its registry of record?
Which state transitions are permitted, who may perform them, and which are irreversible?
Which event caused the most recent state change, and what reason string was recorded?
How must a resolver behave when a required version is yanked or deprecated?
What are the built, released and valid-until instants recorded for this release?
Which release is the recommended replacement, and what migration cost has been recorded?
Which signals indicate this component is no longer actively maintained?
Who is accountable for maintenance now, and has stewardship been transferred?
Which advisories declare this exact version affected, through which range type and events?
How is affectedness computed for a version not explicitly enumerated in the advisory?
When was each advisory published, last modified or withdrawn, and when was this assessment made?
What severity is asserted for each advisory, by which scoring system and which source?
What is the exploitability status of this advisory in the component's actual usage context?
Which remediation was chosen, and who approved it?
What is the fixed version and the concrete upgrade path from the currently adopted version?
Under what documented exception may an affected version remain in use, and until when?
Which health and security-practice checks were run against this component's project, and what results were produced?
Which signals materially change the adoption decision, and what threshold applies?
When were the signals measured, and how quickly do they become stale?
Which tool and tool version produced each signal, and against which repository revision?
What evidence supports the claim that this component is present in the analysed artifact?
What confidence is attached to the identification, and how was that confidence computed?
How are two conflicting identifications of the same artifact reconciled?
Which tool, technique and generation context produced the identification?
From which registry, repository URL and mirrors is this component retrievable, and which is the registry of record?
Which registry's metadata prevails when a public and an internal registry disagree about the same coordinate?
What controls prevent substitution between an internal namespace and a public one with the same name?
Which credentials or entitlements are required to retrieve this component?
How long will this artifact remain retrievable from the registry of record, and under which published policy?
Under which conditions may the publisher remove this release, and may the name and version then be reused?
Which internal copy or archive guarantees continued availability once upstream removal occurs?
What happens to builds already pinned to a version that has been removed upstream?
Who asserted each recorded fact about this component, and from which source document?
How are event time, observation time and ingestion time recorded and distinguished for the same fact?
How stale is each recorded fact, and what refresh obligation applies?
How is a conflicting assertion from two sources resolved and recorded?
Which exchange formats must this component record project into, and at which versions?
Which fields are mandatory in a target format but optional here, and how are the gaps filled?
How is a round-trip projection validated, and what is the acceptance criterion?
Which representation is authoritative when two exported forms of this component disagree?

grok_only.name: What is the canonical Package-URL for this package version?
Which PURL type, namespace, name, version, qualifiers and subpath were parsed from that identifier?
How does this PURL map to the ecosystem-native registry coordinate used by the authoritative package manager?
Which qualifiers select a specific binary, repository mirror, architecture, distro or packaging that is not implied by name and version alone?
What CPE 2.2 URI or CPE 2.3 well-formed name or formatted string identifies the product class of this package?
What SWID tag identifier, tag version and software name identify this software according to ISO/IEC 19770-2?
Does the CPE name identify an abstract product class rather than this unique package instantiation or installed copy?
What SPDX element IRI (spdxId) is assigned to this Package element when it participates in an SPDX graph?
What evidence substantiates the asserted CPE, SWID or PURL identity of this component?
What SWHID identifies the content, directory, revision, release or snapshot corresponding to this package?
Which hash algorithms and digest values uniquely fingerprint the package bytes used as an identity, not merely as a checksum sidecar?
Can the content identifier be recomputed independently from a local copy without consulting a registry?
If a gitoid is present, is it recorded as a SoftwareArtifact contentIdentifier or as an Element externalIdentifier for an OmniBOR input manifest?
What is the authoritative native registry coordinate for this package version, including group or scope, name and version?
What packaging, classifier, type or extension distinguishes this artifact from other artifacts that share the same group, name and version?
Does the native name follow the ecosystem naming convention, such as reversed-domain groupId and lowercase hyphenated artifactId for Maven?
Which organization or namespace is recorded as owning the group, scope or registry namespace of this name?
What version string identifies this released or pre-release package?
Which version scheme is used to parse and compare this version string?
Has the content associated with this version been modified after the version was released, in violation of SemVer immutability or registry policy?
Is this version a pre-release, snapshot, build-metadata-only variant, or a stable release, and how does that affect precedence?
When was this version released or built, and when was that version metadata observed or ingested?
What CycloneDX component type classifies this package?
What SPDX primaryPurpose and additionalPurpose values describe how this package is used?
Is the recorded purpose based on use context rather than bit content, and could the same bits be a library in one product and an application in another?
What publication state applies to this version: released, pre-release, yanked, deprecated, unpublished or withdrawn?
What support level and validity end time apply to this package version?
What builtTime and releaseTime apply as event times, and what observation or ingestion time applies if it differs?
If a SWID tag is aligned, is it a corpus, primary, patch or supplemental tag for this software?
Has this package version been scheduled for decommission or retirement from operations?
What download location or canonical artifact URI locates the distributable bits?
Is retrieval public, authenticated, embargoed or limited to an internal registry?
Which PURL qualifiers or Maven layout segments select a specific repository mirror, architecture, distro or classifier binary?
From which registry or mirror was this copy actually retrieved, and does that differ from the canonical publisher location?
What hash algorithms and values did the publisher or registry declare for this package?
Did verification of a local copy against the declared algorithm and value succeed?
Is a digital signature or additional IntegrityMethod present that binds the package to a publisher key?
What digest was computed at observation or ingestion time, and does it differ from the publisher-declared digest?
Which packages does this package depend on, and with which SPDX or equivalent relationship type?
Which dependencies are direct declarations versus transitive closures, and is the transitive set complete?
What dependency scope applies to each edge, such as compile, provided, runtime, test, required, optional or excluded?
Which dependencies are known unknowns that the author or tooling could not resolve?
During which lifecycle scope does each dependency, link or tool relationship apply?
Which files, sub-packages or expanded artifacts does this package contain or distribute?
Which SBOM documents (WM-SFT-012) describe this package as a component or root?
What relationship completeness is asserted for this package's composition: complete, incomplete, unknown or a CycloneDX composition aggregate?
Is this package the SPDX rootElement or CycloneDX metadata.component of an inventory, or only a nested component?
What pedigree of ancestors, descendants, variants or commits is recorded for this component?
Which agent originated or manufactured this package?
Which agent supplied this copy of the package, and is that party distinct from the originator?
Who is authorized to publish new versions under this registry namespace or group?
What country or postal address is recorded for the supplier or manufacturer organization?
What license identifiers were declared by the authors or the package manifest?
What license identifiers were concluded after analysis, and do they differ from the declared licenses?
What copyright text is asserted for this package?
What observed license evidence inside the artifact supports the concluded license?
Who may read this package's metadata versus download its bits, and under what scope?
If this version is yanked, unpublished or deleted, what identifier, metadata and bits are retained and for how long?
How do PURL, CPE, SWID, SPDX IRI and content hashes align or conflict for this instance, and which identifier is master?
What embargo, private-feed, export-control or legal-hold exceptions override the default access rule?
Given colliding coordinates or renamed namespaces, which identifier should operators treat as the master-system key for this record?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
